findings.message: A single `_sc_rc_file` is shared across the batch call and every per-spec fallback call; if the batch call times out (rc=124) but a subsequent per-spec fallback call succeeds (rc=0), the final `_sc_router_rc` reads 0 and `disposition: complete` is written — the timeout signal is silently lost.

`_scv_rc_file` is created with `mktemp` but no trap is installed; if `spec_coverage_run` exits unexpectedly between the `mktemp` call and the `rm -f` at line 192, the temp file leaks — the same pattern applies to `_sc_rc_file` in `spec-correspondence/plugin.sh`.

When a lens `.rc` file is absent (lens subshell died before writing it), the `|| echo 1` fallback produces rc=1 which `router_reason_disposition` maps to the catch-all `unavailable`; a lens killed by a signal would be classified as `unavailable` rather than `interrupted`, misrepresenting the failure cause in the disposition field.

`cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence` emits only `iter` and `reason=member_did_not_finish`; unlike `cycle.build_unfinished.suppressed_convergence` which also emits `build_verdict`, this event carries no member identity — determining which member triggered suppression requires separately cross-referencing the verdicts blob.

Before this change `review-report` always wrote `disposition: complete` on lens failure; after, it writes `disposition: unavailable` (rc=1) or `timed_out` (rc=124). `unavailable` is NOT in `disposition_unfinished`, so the new cycle suppression does not fire for it — but any engine consumer that applies the ADR-054 §6 response table to this field will now see `halt_unavailable` where it previously saw `proceed`, a net-new halt path for this advisory stage.
